abbreviations.AMTSL: Active management of the third stage of labour
abbreviations.BRa: Baseline rate of the fetal heart (CTG)
abbreviations.BRAN: Consent: Benefits, Risks, Alternatives, doing Nothing
abbreviations.BRAVADO: Baseline Rate, Variability, Accelerations, Decelerations, Overall
abbreviations.CSA: Chondroitin sulphate A (placental receptor that infected red cells stick to)
abbreviations.D&E: Dilatation and evacuation (emptying the uterus with forceps after 14 wk)
abbreviations.DA: Diamniotic: twins in two separate amniotic sacs
abbreviations.DC: Dichorionic: twins with two separate placentas
abbreviations.DR: Define risk (first step of reading a CTG: DR C BRAVADO)
abbreviations.FIGO: International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics
abbreviations.FRC: Functional residual capacity of the lungs
abbreviations.GTD: Gestational trophoblastic disease: moles and related tumours of the placenta
abbreviations.GTN: Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia: persistent or malignant trophoblast after a mole
abbreviations.hCG: Human chorionic gonadotrophin: the pregnancy hormone made by the placenta, measured in blood or urine
abbreviations.HCG: Human chorionic gonadotrophin: the pregnancy hormone made by the placenta
abbreviations.HELLP: Haemolysis, Elevated Liver enzymes, Low Platelets
abbreviations.HELPERR: Help, Evaluate episiotomy, Legs, Pressure, Enter, Remove arm, Roll
abbreviations.ICE: The patient's Ideas, Concerns and Expectations
abbreviations.ICMBA: Liquor codes on the partograph: Intact, Clear, Meconium, Blood, Absent
abbreviations.IgA: Immunoglobulin A (antibody in breast milk and mucosa)
abbreviations.IgM: Immunoglobulin M (antibody of a recent infection)
abbreviations.KOH: Potassium hydroxide (whiff test for bacterial vaginosis)
abbreviations.MP: Mento-posterior (face presentation, chin towards the sacrum)
abbreviations.OASI: Obstetric anal sphincter injury (3rd- or 4th-degree tear)
abbreviations.PaCO₂: Carbon dioxide level in arterial blood (normal 4.7–6 kPa; low in pregnancy, about 4 kPa, because of deeper breathing)
abbreviations.PaO₂: Oxygen level in arterial blood (normal above 10.6 kPa)
abbreviations.PI: Pulsatility index (Doppler measure of resistance to blood flow)
abbreviations.SPIKES: Breaking bad news: Setting, Perception, Invitation, Knowledge, Emotions, Strategy and summary
abbreviations.STV: Short-term variability of the fetal heart rate (computerised CTG)
abbreviations.TLD: Tenofovir + lamivudine + dolutegravir (first-line HIV treatment in one tablet)
abbreviations.VDRL: Venereal Disease Research Laboratory test (screening test for syphilis)
abbreviations.β-hCG: Beta human chorionic gonadotrophin: the pregnancy hormone, measured in blood
abbreviations.NMDA: N-methyl-D-aspartate (a glutamate receptor in the brain)
abbreviations.pCO₂: Partial pressure of carbon dioxide on a blood gas (normal 35–45 mmHg = 4.7–6 kPa; about 30 mmHg in pregnancy)
abbreviations.pO₂: Partial pressure of oxygen on a blood gas (normal 80–100 mmHg = 10.6–13.3 kPa)

MA.mp: Monoamniotic: twins sharing one amniotic sac
MA.*: Mento-anterior (face presentation, chin towards the pubis)

glossary.abruption: Premature separation of a normally sited placenta.
glossary.accelerations: Rises of the fetal heart rate by ≥ 15 bpm for ≥ 15 s; a sign of a healthy fetus.
glossary.accreta: Placenta abnormally stuck into the uterine wall.
glossary.acidosis: Too much acid in the blood (low pH).
glossary.adnexal: Of the structures beside the uterus (tubes and ovaries).
glossary.adrenal: Gland above the kidney that makes cortisol and adrenaline.
glossary.aftercoming: Coming after the body, as the head in a breech delivery.
glossary.agenesis: Failure of an organ to develop.
glossary.alkalosis: Too little acid in the blood (high pH).
glossary.amiodarone: Antiarrhythmic drug; affects the fetal thyroid.
glossary.amniocentesis: Taking amniotic fluid with a needle for testing.
glossary.amniotic: Of the amnion, the membrane sac around the fetus.
glossary.anencephaly: Absent skull vault and brain: lethal neural tube defect.
glossary.aneuploidy: Wrong number of chromosomes in the cells (for example trisomy).
glossary.antifibrinolytic: Drug that stops clot breakdown (e.g. tranexamic acid).
glossary.antiphospholipid: Antiphospholipid syndrome: antibodies causing clots and recurrent miscarriage.
glossary.antiseptic: Substance that kills germs on skin or wounds.
glossary.aortocaval compression: Pregnant uterus presses on the aorta and IVC when supine.
glossary.apgar: Newborn score (0–10) of colour, pulse, reflex, tone, breathing.
glossary.artesunate: Artemisinin drug; IV treatment of choice for severe malaria.
glossary.asherman: Asherman syndrome: scar bands inside the uterus after too much scraping (curettage) or infection; periods become scanty or stop, and fertility falls.
glossary.asphyxia: Lack of oxygen to the baby around birth.
glossary.atelectasis: Collapse of part of a lung.
glossary.atonic: Without tone; uterine atony is the commonest cause of PPH.
glossary.atony: A soft, poorly contracted uterus after birth.
glossary.atresia: Absence or closure of a normal body opening or tube.
glossary.augmentation: Speeding up slow labour, usually with ARM and oxytocin.
glossary.autotransfusion: Blood squeezed back into the circulation by the contracting uterus.
glossary.ballotable: Can be pushed away and floats back: not engaged.
glossary.ballottement: A floating fetal part bounces away and back when tapped.
glossary.betamethasone: Corticosteroid given to mature the fetal lungs.
glossary.bilirubin: Yellow pigment from the breakdown of haemoglobin.
glossary.bimanual: Examination with one hand inside the vagina and one on the abdomen.
glossary.brachial: Of the arm; brachial plexus injury causes Erb's palsy.
glossary.braxton hicks: Painless irregular practice contractions of pregnancy.
glossary.breech: The fetal buttocks or feet present at the pelvis instead of the head.
glossary.cabergoline: Dopamine agonist that stops milk production.
glossary.caesarean: Delivery of the baby through a cut in the abdomen and uterus.
glossary.candida: Yeast causing itchy white curdy discharge.
glossary.cannulae: Plastic tubes placed in a vein for fluids and drugs (singular: cannula).
glossary.caput: Swelling of the fetal scalp from pressure in labour.
glossary.carbamazepine: Antiepileptic drug; risk of neural tube defects.
glossary.carbimazole: Antithyroid drug; avoided in the first trimester.
glossary.carboprost: Prostaglandin F2-alpha given IM for PPH; avoid in asthma.
glossary.catheterise: Pass a tube (catheter) into the bladder.
glossary.caudal: Towards the lower end of the body.
glossary.ceftriaxone: Third-generation cephalosporin antibiotic given IV or IM.
glossary.centile: Position on a growth chart compared with 100 babies.
glossary.cephalhaematoma: Bleeding under the periosteum of a skull bone; does not cross suture lines.
glossary.cephalopelvic disproportion: Baby's head too big for the mother's pelvis.
glossary.cerclage: Stitch around the cervix to keep it closed.
glossary.cervical excitation: Sharp pain when the cervix is moved during vaginal examination: a sign of blood or inflammation in the pelvis.
glossary.chadwick: Bluish vagina and cervix from congestion (≈ 8 wk).
glossary.chaperone: A trained person present during an intimate examination.
glossary.chlamydia: Sexually transmitted bacterium causing cervicitis and neonatal conjunctivitis.
glossary.chloasma: Brown patches on the face in pregnancy (melasma).
glossary.chloramphenicol: Antibiotic avoided near term (grey baby syndrome).
glossary.cholestasis: Bile flow blocked: itching and raised bile acids.
glossary.chorioamnionitis: Infection of the fetal membranes and amniotic fluid.
glossary.choriocarcinoma: Malignant tumour of trophoblast; spreads early to lungs.
glossary.chorion: Outer fetal membrane; forms the placenta.
glossary.chorionicity: Number of placentas (chorions) in a twin pregnancy.
glossary.clindamycin: Antibiotic used for bacterial vaginosis and in penicillin allergy.
glossary.clonus: Repeated jerking of the foot when dorsiflexed: brain irritability.
glossary.co-amoxiclav: Amoxicillin with clavulanic acid; avoided in preterm rupture of membranes (NEC risk).
glossary.colicky: Pain that comes and goes in waves.
glossary.colostrum: Thick yellow first milk, rich in antibodies.
glossary.conjugate: A diameter of the pelvic inlet (true and diagonal conjugate).
glossary.contraindicated: Must not be used in that situation.
glossary.contraindication: A reason a treatment must not be used.
glossary.cord prolapse: Umbilical cord slips below the presenting part after membranes rupture.
glossary.corpus luteum: Ovarian structure making progesterone in early pregnancy.
glossary.cotyledon: A lobe on the maternal surface of the placenta.
glossary.couvelaire: Couvelaire uterus: blood tracking into the uterine muscle in severe abruption.
glossary.crackles: Fine sounds heard over the lungs when fluid is in the alveoli.
glossary.creatinine: Waste product cleared by the kidneys; used to measure kidney function.
glossary.crown-rump length: Length of the embryo from head to bottom: best dating.
glossary.crowning: Fetal head stays visible at the vulva between contractions.
glossary.crystalloid: Clear IV fluid such as normal saline or Ringer's lactate.
glossary.cyanosis: Blue colour of skin or lips from low oxygen.
glossary.deceleration: Temporary fall in fetal heart rate on CTG.
glossary.decidua: The lining of the uterus in pregnancy.
glossary.decompensate: Organ can no longer cope; symptoms appear.
glossary.deflexed: Head not well flexed, so a larger diameter presents.
glossary.deinfibulation: Opening an infibulated (type III FGC) scar.
glossary.denominator: Fixed point on the presenting part used to name the position (e.g. occiput).
glossary.dexamethasone: Corticosteroid given to mature the fetal lungs before preterm birth.
glossary.diastolic: The pressure or murmur during heart relaxation.
glossary.dilatation: Opening of the cervix, measured in cm (0–10).
glossary.dinoprostone: Prostaglandin E2 used to ripen the cervix.
glossary.dipstick: Test strip for urine (protein, glucose, ketones, blood, nitrites).
glossary.discriminatory zone: The hCG level (about 1500–2000 IU/L) above which a pregnancy inside the uterus should be seen on transvaginal scan.
glossary.ductus: Ductus arteriosus: fetal vessel joining the pulmonary artery to the aorta.
glossary.ductus arteriosus: Fetal vessel joining the pulmonary artery to the aorta.
glossary.ebstein anomaly: Heart defect of the tricuspid valve (lithium).
glossary.eclampsia: Fits in a woman with pre-eclampsia.
glossary.ectopic: Pregnancy implanted outside the uterine cavity (usually tube).
glossary.ectropion: Red columnar epithelium on the outer cervix.
glossary.effacement: Thinning and shortening of the cervix in labour.
glossary.eisenmenger: Eisenmenger syndrome: reversed shunt with pulmonary hypertension; very high maternal mortality.
glossary.electrophoresis: Laboratory test that separates haemoglobin types (sickle cell, thalassaemia).
glossary.embolism: Blockage of a vessel by a clot or other material carried in the blood.
glossary.embryopathy: Damage to the embryo, usually by a drug or infection.
glossary.enalapril: ACE inhibitor; avoid in pregnancy, safe in breastfeeding.
glossary.endometritis: Infection of the lining of the uterus, usually after birth.
glossary.engagement: The widest part of the presenting part has passed the pelvic brim.
glossary.engorgement: Overfull, hard, painful breasts as milk comes in.
glossary.epidural: Local anaesthetic injected into the epidural space of the spine to relieve labour pain.
glossary.epigastric: Upper middle abdomen, below the breastbone.
glossary.epilepticus: Status epilepticus: a fit lasting > 5 minutes or fits without recovery between them.
glossary.episiotomy: Planned cut of the perineum to enlarge the outlet at birth.
glossary.ergometrine: Drug that causes a sustained uterine contraction; used for PPH; raises blood pressure.
glossary.erythromycin: Macrolide antibiotic; used after preterm rupture of membranes.
glossary.expectant: Watching and waiting without active treatment.
glossary.external cephalic version: Turning a breech baby to head-down from outside the abdomen.
glossary.ferning: Fern pattern of dried liquor under a microscope: membranes ruptured.
glossary.ferrous: Iron salt used as oral iron (ferrous sulphate, fumarate, gluconate).
glossary.fibrinogen: Clotting protein; falls fast in major haemorrhage or DIC.
glossary.fistula: Abnormal passage between two organs (for example bladder and vagina).
glossary.flexion: Bending; in labour, the chin tucks onto the chest so the smallest head diameter leads.
glossary.flucloxacillin: Penicillin for staphylococcal infection (mastitis, wound infection).
glossary.folate: Folic acid (vitamin B9); prevents neural tube defects and megaloblastic anaemia.
glossary.fontanelle: Soft membranous gap between fetal skull bones.
glossary.footling: Breech with one or both feet presenting below the buttocks.
glossary.forceps: Paired metal blades applied to the fetal head to assist delivery.
glossary.fornix: Recess of the vagina around the cervix.
glossary.fourchette: The fold of skin at the back of the vaginal opening.
glossary.fundal height: Distance from the symphysis pubis to the top of the uterus.
glossary.fundus: The top (dome) of the uterus, above the openings of the fallopian tubes.
glossary.furosemide: Loop diuretic; removes fluid in pulmonary oedema.
glossary.galactosaemia: Inherited inability to digest galactose; breastfeeding is contraindicated.
glossary.gestation: Length of pregnancy, from the LMP.
glossary.gonadotrophin: Hormone that stimulates the ovaries or testes (hCG, LH, FSH).
glossary.goodell: Softening of the cervix in pregnancy.
glossary.grand multipara: A woman with 5 or more previous births.
glossary.grimace: Facial response to stimulation (part of the Apgar score).
glossary.growth restriction: Fetus not reaching its growth potential.
glossary.haematoma: Collection of blood in the tissues.
glossary.haemodilution: Blood diluted by extra plasma: Hb falls.
glossary.haemoglobinuria: Haemoglobin in the urine from broken red cells: the urine looks dark red-brown.
glossary.heartburn: Burning pain behind the sternum from acid reflux.
glossary.hegar: Soft isthmus of the uterus at 6–10 weeks.
glossary.heparin: Injectable anticoagulant that does not cross the placenta.
glossary.hookworm: Intestinal worm that sucks blood and causes iron deficiency anaemia.
glossary.hydatidiform mole: Abnormal pregnancy of swollen chorionic villi; very high hCG.
glossary.hydralazine: Vasodilator given IV for severe hypertension in pregnancy.
glossary.hydrocephalus: Excess fluid in the brain ventricles with an enlarged head.
glossary.hydrops: Fluid in two or more fetal body spaces (skin, chest, abdomen).
glossary.hypercoagulable: Blood clots more easily than normal.
glossary.hyperemesis: Severe vomiting in pregnancy with dehydration and weight loss.
glossary.hyperstimulation: Too many or too long contractions, usually from oxytocin or prostaglandins.
glossary.hypovolaemic: From loss of blood or fluid volume.
glossary.hypoxia: Shortage of oxygen in the tissues.
glossary.implantation: Embryo attaching to the uterine lining (day 6–10).
glossary.incontinence: Inability to hold urine or faeces.
glossary.indomethacin: NSAID used as a tocolytic before 32 weeks.
glossary.infibulation: FGC type III: labia cut and sewn with a small opening.
glossary.involution: Return of the uterus to its non-pregnant size after birth.
glossary.ischial: Of the ischium, the lower bone of the pelvis (ischial spines, tuberosities).
glossary.isoimmunisation: Mother makes antibodies against fetal red cells.
glossary.isthmus: The narrow part of the uterus between body and cervix; forms the lower segment.
glossary.jarisch–herxheimer: Fever and flu-like reaction after treating syphilis.
glossary.jaundice: Yellow colour of skin and eyes from raised bilirubin.
glossary.ketones: Acids made when fat is burnt for energy (starvation, vomiting, DKA).
glossary.ketonuria: Ketones in urine: body burning fat (starving, vomiting).
glossary.kielland: Rotational forceps used to turn the fetal head.
glossary.kleihauer: Blood test counting fetal cells in the mother's blood.
glossary.labetalol: Alpha- and beta-blocker; first-line drug for hypertension in pregnancy.
glossary.lactate: Product of anaerobic metabolism; a high level shows poor tissue perfusion.
glossary.lactational amenorrhoea: No periods while fully breastfeeding: natural contraception.
glossary.lambda sign: Thick triangular membrane junction on scan: dichorionic twins.
glossary.lamotrigine: Antiepileptic drug with a low risk of fetal malformation.
glossary.laparoscopy: Keyhole surgery: a camera and instruments passed through small cuts in the abdomen.
glossary.laparotomy: Open abdominal surgery through a cut in the abdominal wall.
glossary.leucorrhoea: White vaginal discharge (normal more in pregnancy).
glossary.levetiracetam: Antiepileptic drug with a low risk of fetal malformation.
glossary.ligation: Tying off a vessel or tube.
glossary.lightening: The fetal head drops into the pelvis near term; fundus falls.
glossary.linea nigra: Dark line down the middle of the abdomen in pregnancy.
glossary.liquor: The amniotic fluid around the fetus.
glossary.lithotomy: Lying on the back with hips and knees bent and legs apart.
glossary.lochia: Vaginal discharge after birth (blood, decidua, mucus).
glossary.lower segment: Thin lower part of the uterus in late pregnancy; site of usual CS.
glossary.macrosomia: Big baby: birth weight > 4 kg (or > 4.5 kg).
glossary.malposition: Vertex but not occipito-anterior (e.g. OP, OT).
glossary.malpresentation: Any presentation other than vertex (breech, face, brow, shoulder).
glossary.marfan: Marfan syndrome: connective tissue disorder with risk of aortic dissection.
glossary.mastitis: Inflammation or infection of the breast.
glossary.mauriceau: Mauriceau–Smellie–Veit manoeuvre: delivers the aftercoming head in breech.
glossary.mcdonald: McDonald stitch: a purse-string stitch around the cervix placed through the vagina; quick to put in and easy to remove.
glossary.meconium: Baby's first stool; in liquor may mean fetal stress.
glossary.meconium-stained: Coloured green by fetal stool passed into the amniotic fluid.
glossary.mediolateral: Directed downwards and outwards from the midline (episiotomy).
glossary.megaloblastic: Anaemia with large red cells from folate or vitamin B12 deficiency.
glossary.mento-posterior: Face presentation with the chin towards the sacrum.
glossary.mento-vertical: Chin-to-vertex diameter (13.5 cm); presents in brow presentation.
glossary.metformin: Oral drug for diabetes; safe in pregnancy.
glossary.methotrexate: Folic acid antagonist; dissolves an unruptured ectopic pregnancy.
glossary.methyldopa: Centrally acting drug for hypertension in pregnancy.
glossary.metoclopramide: Antiemetic that empties the stomach; can cause dystonia.
glossary.metronidazole: Antibiotic for anaerobes, bacterial vaginosis and trichomonas.
glossary.microvesicular: Fat in small droplets within liver cells (acute fatty liver of pregnancy).
glossary.midstream: Midstream urine: a sample taken from the middle of the stream for culture.
glossary.mifepristone: Antiprogesterone tablet given before misoprostol to empty the uterus.
glossary.misoprostol: Prostaglandin E1 tablet used to ripen the cervix, induce labour, empty the uterus and treat PPH.
glossary.mitral: The valve between left atrium and left ventricle.
glossary.mitral stenosis: Narrow mitral valve, usually from rheumatic fever.
glossary.molar: Abnormal placenta (hydatidiform mole) with swollen villi, high hCG.
glossary.mole: Hydatidiform mole: abnormal pregnancy where the placenta grows into grape-like fluid sacs, usually with no normal fetus.
glossary.montgomery tubercles: Small bumps on the areola in pregnancy.
glossary.moulding: Overlapping of fetal skull bones during labour.
glossary.mucosa: Moist lining of a hollow organ.
glossary.multipara: A woman who has given birth (≥ 24 wk) more than once.
glossary.murmur: Sound of turbulent blood flow heard over the heart.
glossary.möbius syndrome: Facial nerve palsy defect linked to misoprostol misuse.
glossary.neuroprotection: Protecting the preterm baby's brain (MgSO₄ < 32 wk).
glossary.nifedipine: Calcium-channel blocker; lowers blood pressure and relaxes the uterus.
glossary.nitrazine: pH paper that turns blue with alkaline liquor.
glossary.nitrite: Product of bacteria in urine; positive dipstick suggests infection.
glossary.nitrofurantoin: Antibiotic for urinary infection; avoid near term.
glossary.nuchal translucency: Fluid behind the fetal neck on 11–14 wk scan.
glossary.nullipara: A woman who has never given birth at ≥ 24 weeks.
glossary.obstructed: Blocked; obstructed labour = no progress despite good contractions because the passage is too small.
glossary.occipito-frontal: Occiput-to-forehead diameter (11.5 cm); presents in occipito-posterior positions.
glossary.occiput: Back of the fetal skull: the denominator in vertex presentations.
glossary.oedema: Swelling caused by excess fluid in the tissues.
glossary.oligohydramnios: Too little amniotic fluid for the gestation (AFI < 5 cm).
glossary.organogenesis: Formation of organs: weeks 3–8 after conception.
glossary.ovulation: Release of an egg from the ovary.
glossary.oxytocin: Posterior pituitary hormone that makes the uterus contract and ejects milk; given as a drug to induce labour and prevent PPH.
glossary.pallor: Paleness of skin or conjunctiva; a sign of anaemia.
glossary.paracervical block: Local anaesthetic injected beside the cervix to numb it before an MVA or dilatation.
glossary.partogram: Chart that plots labour progress, fetal and maternal condition.
glossary.partograph: Chart that plots labour progress, fetal and maternal condition.
glossary.pathophysiology: How a disease disturbs normal body function.
glossary.percreta: Placenta percreta: placenta invading through the uterine wall.
glossary.perforation: A hole through the wall of an organ.
glossary.perimortem: At the time of death; perimortem caesarean is done within 4 minutes of maternal arrest.
glossary.perinatal: Around birth: from 22–24 wk of pregnancy to 7 days after birth.
glossary.perineum: Tissue between the vaginal opening and the anus.
glossary.pfannenstiel: Low transverse skin incision above the pubic hair.
glossary.phenytoin: Antiepileptic drug; causes fetal hydantoin syndrome.
glossary.pinard: Trumpet-shaped stethoscope for listening to the fetal heart.
glossary.pitting: A dent stays after pressing on swollen skin.
glossary.pituitary: Gland at the base of the brain that controls other glands.
glossary.placenta praevia: Placenta implanted in the lower uterine segment.
glossary.platelets: Small blood cells that start clotting.
glossary.pleuritic: Sharp chest pain worse on breathing in.
glossary.polyhydramnios: Too much amniotic fluid (AFI > 24–25 cm or deepest pool > 8 cm).
glossary.pooling: Collection of amniotic fluid in the posterior fornix seen on speculum examination.
glossary.postmaturity: Signs in a baby born after 42 weeks (dry peeling skin, long nails, meconium).
glossary.praevia: Placenta lying in the lower segment, near or over the os.
glossary.pre-eclampsia: New hypertension after 20 wk with proteinuria or organ damage.
glossary.presenting part: The part of the fetus lowest in the birth canal.
glossary.primaquine: Antimalarial; avoid in pregnancy and G6PD deficiency.
glossary.primigravida: A woman pregnant for the first time.
glossary.priming: Softening and opening the cervix with a drug (misoprostol) before an operation, so instruments pass easily and the cervix tears less.
glossary.prolactin: Pituitary hormone that makes the breast produce milk.
glossary.prolapse: Slipping down of a structure from its normal position (for example cord prolapse).
glossary.prophylaxis: Treatment given to prevent a disease.
glossary.prostaglandin: Hormone-like substance that ripens the cervix and contracts the uterus.
glossary.prostin: Dinoprostone (PGE2) vaginal gel or tablet to ripen the cervix.
glossary.pseudocyesis: False belief of pregnancy with symptoms but no pregnancy.
glossary.psychosis: Loss of contact with reality: hallucinations, delusions.
glossary.puerperal: Related to the 6 weeks after birth.
glossary.puerperium: The 6 weeks after delivery of the placenta.
glossary.quickening: The first fetal movements the mother feels.
glossary.radioiodine: Radioactive iodine; never given in pregnancy.
glossary.red degeneration: Painful necrosis of a fibroid in pregnancy.
glossary.restitution: The head turns back to line up with the shoulders after birth.
glossary.resuscitation: Emergency restoration of breathing and circulation.
glossary.retained placenta: Placenta not delivered 30 min after the baby (with AMTSL).
glossary.rheumatic: Related to rheumatic fever, which damages the heart valves.
glossary.ripening: Softening and opening of the cervix before labour.
glossary.rubella: German measles; causes congenital malformations in early pregnancy.
glossary.sacrum: Triangular bone at the back of the pelvis.
glossary.sagittal: In the midline from front to back (sagittal suture of the skull).
glossary.salpingotomy: Opening the tube to remove the ectopic pregnancy while keeping the tube; hCG is followed afterwards in case tissue is left.
glossary.schistosomiasis: Parasitic worm infection (bilharzia) causing anaemia and haematuria.
glossary.sertraline: SSRI antidepressant; preferred in pregnancy and breastfeeding.
glossary.sheehan: Pituitary necrosis after massive PPH: no milk, no periods.
glossary.shirodkar: Shirodkar stitch: a cervical stitch placed higher, near the internal os, after pushing the bladder up; stronger but harder to remove.
glossary.shoulder dystocia: Shoulders stuck after the head is born.
glossary.sinciput: Front part of the fetal skull (forehead area).
glossary.sinusoidal: Smooth wave-like CTG pattern; suggests severe fetal anaemia.
glossary.snowstorm: Snowstorm pattern: the scan picture of a complete mole, many small fluid spaces like falling snow, with no fetus.
glossary.speculum: Instrument that holds the vaginal walls apart so the cervix can be seen.
glossary.sphincter: Ring of muscle that closes an opening.
glossary.spina bifida: Neural tube defect of the spine.
glossary.squames: Flat fetal skin cells; found in maternal blood in amniotic fluid embolism.
glossary.stillbirth: Birth of a baby with no signs of life after 28 weeks (WHO) or 24 weeks (UK).
glossary.subcuticular: Just under the skin surface (continuous skin suture).
glossary.subinvolution: Uterus shrinking more slowly than normal after birth.
glossary.submento-bregmatic: Under-chin to bregma diameter (9.5 cm); presents in face presentation.
glossary.suboccipito-bregmatic: Below-occiput to bregma diameter (9.5 cm); the smallest, presents when the head is well flexed.
glossary.succenturiate lobe: An extra placental lobe joined by vessels to the main placenta.
glossary.suckling: The baby sucking at the breast.
glossary.supine hypotension: Low BP when lying flat in late pregnancy.
glossary.surfactant: Lung substance that keeps alveoli open; steroids increase it.
glossary.sutures: 1. Stitches. 2. Fibrous joints between the bones of the fetal skull.
glossary.symphysiotomy: Cutting the symphysis pubis to enlarge the pelvis (last resort in shoulder dystocia).
glossary.symphysis: The joint between the two pubic bones at the front of the pelvis.
glossary.syncytiotrophoblast: Outer placental layer that makes hCG and hPL.
glossary.systolic: The pressure or murmur during heart contraction.
glossary.tamponade: Pressure applied inside a cavity to stop bleeding (for example a balloon in the uterus).
glossary.teratogen: Drug or agent that causes birth defects.
glossary.terbutaline: Beta-2 agonist that relaxes the uterus (acute tocolysis).
glossary.tetanus: Infection by Clostridium tetani causing muscle spasms; prevented by vaccination.
glossary.tetracycline: Antibiotic avoided in pregnancy because it stains fetal teeth.
glossary.thalassaemia: Inherited disorder of haemoglobin chains causing microcytic anaemia.
glossary.theca lutein cysts: Large ovarian cysts caused by very high hCG (mole, twins); they shrink once hCG falls.
glossary.thiamine: Vitamin B1; given before glucose in hyperemesis to prevent Wernicke's encephalopathy.
glossary.thrombin: Clotting enzyme; 'Thrombin' in the 4 Ts of PPH means a clotting disorder.
glossary.thromboembolism: A clot that forms in a vein and may travel to the lungs.
glossary.thrombophilia: Inherited or acquired tendency to form clots.
glossary.thrombophlebitis: Clot with inflammation in a superficial vein.
glossary.thromboprophylaxis: Drugs or measures to prevent clots (e.g. LMWH).
glossary.thrombosis: Formation of a blood clot inside a vessel.
glossary.tocolysis: Using drugs to stop or slow uterine contractions.
glossary.tocolytic: A drug that relaxes the uterus.
glossary.torsion: Twisting (e.g. of an ovary) cutting its blood supply.
glossary.tranexamic: Tranexamic acid: drug that stops clots from breaking down; reduces bleeding.
glossary.trichomonas: Protozoan causing frothy, itchy vaginal discharge.
glossary.trimesters: The three thirds of pregnancy (to 13, 27 and 40 weeks).
glossary.trophoblast: Outer cells of the embryo that form the placenta.
glossary.umbilical artery: Artery in the cord; its Doppler shows placental resistance.
glossary.unfavourable: A cervix not ready for labour (low Bishop score).
glossary.ureters: Tubes that carry urine from the kidneys to the bladder.
glossary.ursodeoxycholic: Ursodeoxycholic acid: bile acid that relieves itching in obstetric cholestasis.
glossary.uterotonic: A drug that makes the uterus contract (e.g. oxytocin).
glossary.vaginosis: Bacterial vaginosis: overgrowth of anaerobes with grey fishy discharge.
glossary.valproate: Antiepileptic drug with the highest risk of fetal malformation.
glossary.vasa praevia: Fetal vessels run in the membranes over the cervix.
glossary.vasopressors: Drugs that raise blood pressure by constricting vessels.
glossary.vasospasm: Narrowing of blood vessels by muscle spasm.
glossary.velamentous: Cord inserted into the membranes, not the placenta.
glossary.ventouse: Vacuum cup applied to the baby's head to assist delivery.
glossary.vertex: Area of the fetal skull between the fontanelles and parietal eminences.
glossary.viability: Age from which a fetus can survive outside the womb (24 wk here).
glossary.villi: Finger-like placental projections where exchange happens.
glossary.warfarin: Oral anticoagulant (vitamin K antagonist); harms the fetus in early pregnancy.
glossary.wernicke: Brain damage from thiamine deficiency: confusion, ataxia, eye signs.
glossary.wheeze: Whistling breath sound from narrowed airways.
glossary.xiphisternum: The lower tip of the breastbone.
glossary.zidovudine: Antiretroviral drug (AZT); used for infant HIV prophylaxis.
